text:
maria: Starting bring-up for ap-south2 cluster (EKS-managed control plane) with mixed nodepools: cpu-spot (m5.large) and gpu-on-demand (g4dn.12xlarge). Outline below — need quick sanity check :rocket:

maria: Plan:
- create control plane in ap-south2
- nodegroups via eksctl/terraform
- install base addons: aws-node, coredns, kube-proxy, metrics-server, cluster-autoscaler
- GPU DaemonSet (NVIDIA device plugin + driver container) on gpu nodepool
- network policy with Calico
- enable cluster logging to CloudWatch

jiwoo: quick Q — are we using AWS VPC CNI or Cilium? ap-south2 has ENI limits per instance class.

maria: AWS VPC CNI. We'll set warm pool and secondary IPs. For g4dn we checked ENI/ip limits — still need a support quota bump if we exceed 50 GPUs

ashley: make sure to request EC2 quota increases for G4 instances ASAP. Also confirm service quotas for EBS gp3 in region.

samir: FYI I hit a mismatch earlier where kubelet kube-reserved wasn't set on gpu nodes and OOMs happened. Suggest nodegroup user-data includes:

```
# cloud-init snippet
sudo mkdir -p /etc/systemd/system/kubelet.service.d
cat <<'EOF' > /etc/systemd/system/kubelet.service.d/20-reserved.conf
[Service]
Environment="KUBELET_EXTRA_ARGS=--kube-reserved=cpu=500m,memory=512Mi --system-reserved=cpu=200m,memory=256Mi"
EOF
```

maria: Good call. Also we'll taint gpu nodes as `nvidia.io/gpu=true:NoSchedule` and use tolerations on GPU workloads.

jiwoo: Any plan for GPU drivers? We use the Nvidia driver installer DaemonSet with initContainer and host modules. Sample helm install:

```
helm repo add nvidia https://nvidia.github.io/gpu-operator
helm upgrade --install gpu-operator nvidia/gpu-operator --namespace gpu-operator --create-namespace
```

ashley: For validation, run:
- `kubectl get nodes -o wide` (check labels/taints)
- `kubectl describe ds nvidia-driver -n gpu-operator` (ensure host driver present)
- `nvidia-smi` on a pod (run `kubectl run --rm -it --restart=Never --image=nvidia/cuda:11.7-base test-nv -- nvidia-smi`)

maria: Networking validation: ping between pods across AZs, and verify CNI metrics. If Pod IP allocation fails, check ENI config and aws-node logs.

infra-bot: Reminder: regional quota alert — EC2 G4 limit at 48/50; create support ticket 13982 to increase to 200. (automated)

samir: I pushed eksctl config to infra repo under `clusters/ap-south2/eks.yaml`. Nodegroups config:

```
nodeGroups:
  - name: cpu-spot
    instanceType: m5.large
    desiredCapacity: 4
    labels: {role: worker, pool: cpu}
  - name: gpu-on-demand
    instanceType: g4dn.12xlarge
    desiredCapacity: 2
    taints: [{key: "nvidia.io/gpu", value: "true", effect: "NO_SCHEDULE"}]
```

jiwoo: Can we use mixed instances for GPU to save costs? spot is risky for long training jobs. Ops prefers on-demand for prod.

maria: Yes — spot for ephemeral batch, on-demand for steady inference nodes.

ashley: Handoff checklist for SRE oncall:
- confirm control plane health (kubectl get cs)
- ensure node autoscaler policy exists and scaling tests passed
- run 3 synthetic inference requests to verify end-to-end latency under 95th pct targets
- add runbook link: https://wiki.internal.redwood/infra/ap-south2

jiwoo: small nit: set `cluster-autoscaler` to respect node taints with `--expander=least-waste` and `--balance-similar-node-groups` flags.

maria: Ok I'm going to start cluster creation now. Will post the eksctl output and first `kubectl get nodes` in 10-15m. @samir @ashley please watch quotas and driver rollout :eyes:

ashley: on it. I'll open the EC2 quota ticket and DM oncall if we need emergency increases. :thumbsup:

maria: UPDATE (1795002300): control plane created. `eksctl utils write-kubeconfig --region ap-south2 --cluster redwood-ap-south2` done.

maria: UPDATE (1795002475): nodegroups provisioning. cpu-spot nodes joined; gpu-on-demand stuck in `NotReady` — `kubelet` reporting `failed to register with cni: no available network config`

samir: suspect aws-node timing; check `kubectl logs -n kube-system daemonset/aws-node` and `describe pod` — also confirm IAM role for node has `ec2:AssignPrivateIpAddresses` permission

jiwoo: I saw that before — the solution was to bump `--eni-max-pods-per-node` config in aws-node config map for the instance type, and ensure valid `amazon-vpc-cni-k8s` plugin version.

maria: Fix applied, nodes now `Ready` at 1795002589. Installing GPU operator next.

maria: Final notes for handoff:
- infra repo PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pull/512
- open issues: quota ticket 13982 (pending), metrics-server clusterRole warnings
- owner: maria (bootstrap), samir (node config), jiwoo (networking)

ashley: thanks — will mark this cluster as `staging` and run cost smoke test tomorrow. :white_check_mark:

maria: Thanks team. Closing check-in.
